content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text decides whether cited verses count as unanswered witnesses against D2 vs C3 and regrades the link based on an asserted retraction.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"the line is cured by retraction, not defended: every witness pressed against C3 was named and answered in the challenger's own later rounds ((DR2) §C and (DR3) C3 quoting Matthew 1:18, 1:25 and Deuteronomy 22:24; (DR3) C4 quoting Luke 1:34), so the \"witness left unanswered\" ground fails","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.","room":"If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it: reading one, an answered verse cannot be counted as an unanswered witness; reading two, the formal pressing-quote requirement still controls even when the judge says answered. I used reading one.","why":"The judge says the witnesses were answered in later rounds and therefore does not count them, leaving no link BROKEN, which is exactly what K-G4 permits when a verse is answered."}
